transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-05
Time: 15:00 PT (PDT)
Duration: 55 min
Attendees: Adam Reed (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Marta Alvarez (Silverline - Head of Data Privacy); Samir Patel (Silverline - Lead Platform Eng); Janelle Chu (Silverline - Compliance); Michael O'Neal (Silverline CTO)
Links shared: redwood_compliance_deck.pdf, preliminary-benchmark.xlsx, private-deploy-guide.md

Summary:
15:00 - quick intros and goals - map compliance evidence + constraints, decide host/dedicated/private feasibility

Topics:
- Primary regs: GDPR (EUD), UK-DPA, FINRA-ish reporting, and potential HIPAA scoping for a new health-vertical product
- Logging: what we store, retention windows, redaction (PII), access controls, encryption at rest/in transit
- Deployment modes: hosted with region locking, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private VPC/on-prem
- Evidence & audit-ready exports: format, chain-of-custody, who signs off

Transcript:
[00:00] Adam Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick round-robin — I'm Adam, AE on Redwood, with Priya our SE and Lena from customer success. Marta, do you want to lead with the why for today's chat?
[00:18] Marta Alvarez: Yeah hi — thanks. So Silverline's preparing to spin up an LLM-powered compliance-assist feature for our institutional clients, and our audit team wants to know: can we prove where data lived, how logs were retained, and show evidence to FINRA-style auditors. We're also juggling GDPR DSARs and a potential HIPAA interplay. So trying to map options: hosted, dedicated, or fully private.
[00:43] Priya Nair: Great, that's exactly the kind of scope we help model. First clarifying question — do you have any regulatory constraints that require on-prem or is cloud region locking acceptable? In other words, is the barrier data residency or cert-level isolation?
[01:06] Samir Patel: Right now cloud is fine, but the legal team insists that production PII must never leave eu-west for EU customers, and US financial workloads need logs retained for seven years per our retention policy. Also, some auditors want the full raw request/response logs, others only hashed payloads — depends on the case.
[01:31] Janelle Chu: And to add, for certain clients we need attestations that keys are customer-managed via KMS/HSM so we can show key custody separation.
[01:42] Adam Reed: Understood. High level — Redwood hosted can be region-locked so your tenant is pinned to eu-west-1 and us-east-1, but Hosted does keep some control-plane telemetry in our backend; we do offer options to limit what is persisted. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in your tenancy with stricter separation and more fine-grained log controls, and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane.
[02:15] Michael O'Neal: When you say "control-plane telemetry" — can you give examples? Are we talking metrics and anonymized traces or request payloads?
[02:27] Priya Nair: Mostly metrics, orchestration traces, and runtime health; request and full prompt data are considered customer data and by default are stored per your retention settings. That said, we can configure no-persist for content on Dedicated/Private but that has tradeoffs — e.g., you lose KV cache warm start benefits and some batching optimizations which can affect latency/cost.
[03:00] Marta Alvarez: "No-persist" sounds promising but auditors want chain-of-custody — how do you prove logs weren't modified? Is there an immutable export or signed evidence?
[03:14] Priya Nair: We have an audit export that zips logs with a manifest and a signing hash. For Dedicated/Private, the manifests can be generated in-customer infra and signed with your KMS key, or we can provide a Redwood-signed artifact for hosted. There's occasional confusion: our signed exports are not the same as H S M-signed hardware attestation but they do include a tamper-evident hash chain.
[03:46] Samir Patel: We're going to need the option to redact PII before logs are exported — can Redwood do field-level redaction in the runtime? Like strip or mask account numbers, SSNs, etc.
[04:00] Priya Nair: Yes, we support configurable redaction rules pre-export, plus anonymization hooks that run in the serving path. One caveat — pre-export redaction affects your ability to replay the exact raw prompt if an auditor requests it; we often recommend maintaining a hashed token mapping for reproducibility while never storing raw PII.
[04:26] Janelle Chu: For GDPR DSARs, we need the ability to locate all data tied to an identifier and purge it. Does Redwood support selective deletion across caches and logs?
[04:39] Adam Reed: We support DSAR workflows — deletion across persistent logs and object stores, and a KV invalidation endpoint to purge cached keys. On Hosted we can perform deletions for you if you authorise but we can also provide API endpoints so you can automate it from your side on Dedicated/Private.
[05:00] Speaker 3: Uh — quick question, what's the retention cap on hosted? I thought there was a default 30 days?
[05:10] Adam Reed: Default is 30 days for ephemeral logs on Hosted, but we can extend retention on a contract basis to meet regulatory needs — including multi-year retention for financials. That said, storing multi-year raw prompts increases costs and we often recommend summarization/payload hashing for long-term storage.
[05:34] Marta Alvarez: Can you describe DR and region-failover? Auditors expect continuity plans and proof data never left jurisdiction even during failover.
[05:46] Priya Nair: For region-failover we do cross-region replication only if you opt in. There is an explicit 'region-lock' feature — if enabled, it prevents automatic failover out of region and requires manual approval. That's often used by customers with strict residency requirements.
[06:10] Samir Patel: Network: if we go Dedicated or Private, what's the common pattern for VPC peering or private link? Are you using S3 endpoints for logs, or do logs pass back to Redwood first?
[06:25] Priya Nair: Dedicated and Private typically keep all traffic in your VPC; logs can be written to customer S3 buckets via VPC endpoints so Redwood doesn't see raw logs. For Hosted, logs usually land in Redwood-managed storage unless you elect a cross-account delivery. We'll provide a network checklist.
[06:45] Adam Reed: I'll attach a VPC checklist. Also note for Private on-prem installs, the audit artifacts are entirely customer-managed.
[06:55] Michael O'Neal: What about certs and compliance evidence? Our auditors will ask for SOC2 reports, pen test results, and software bill-of-materials.
[07:06] Adam Reed: We can share our SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summaries. SBOMs — we provide high-level SBOMs for runtime components; detailed SBOMs are available under NDA for Private customers.
[07:24] Marta Alvarez: For HIPAA — if we expand to that health product — we'd need BAA. Do you offer BAAs?
[07:32] Adam Reed: Yes, BAAs are available for Dedicated and Private customers; Hosted can be covered depending on data flows, but Dedicated/Private is the usual route for PHI workloads.
[07:47] Janelle Chu: A few nitty gritty items auditors ask: time synch and signed logs for event correlation, RBAC audit trail — can you map tokens to users and store who triggered what?
[07:59] Priya Nair: We emit correlated audit events with ISO timestamps and a unique request id. For RBAC we integrate with SSO (SAML/OIDC) and produce admin action logs. There is a small mismatch sometimes around naming: our admin audit logs are separate from per-request logs, auditors sometimes want a single bundle; we can produce a combined export.
[08:30] Samir Patel: On keys — you said KMS integration, but can we bring our own HSM? We want customer-held master keys.
[08:40] Priya Nair: For Dedicated we support CMEK via your cloud KMS, and Private on-prem can integrate with HSMs. For Hosted, we offer customer-managed keys via cross-account KMS setup in some cases.
[08:56] Marta Alvarez: Ok, about evidence forms — auditors want CSV with user-id, timestamp, request-id, redacted-prompt, model-version, response-hash. Is that output standard?
[09:08] Adam Reed: We can deliver that as a default export format. Some clients request JSON lines for ingest into their SIEM. We can do both.
[09:20] Speaker 2: There's also concern about model provenance — auditors ask which model version and quantization were used.
[09:28] Priya Nair: We log model metadata (version, quantization, runtime flags) with each request so you can show exact configuration. Note mislabeling can happen if models are rolled — we recommend pinning model versions for regulated workloads.
[09:48] Marta Alvarez: Good. On the subject of redaction — can the redaction rules be reviewed by our compliance team? They want to ensure the regexes are strict enough.
[09:58] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We can provide a rule preview tool and a staging export so your team can validate before enabling in prod.
[10:10] Samir Patel: If we wanted zero-retention for certain clients but still provide auditors with evidence, is there a recommended pattern?
[10:20] Priya Nair: Common pattern: keep hashed mappings and signed manifests; optionally keep minimal metadata required for auditing (timestamps, model-version, request-id) while redacting content. For deeper audits, customers sometimes perform in-scope reproduction runs in a secure environment with consented replays.
[10:42] Janelle Chu: About access — we need log access controls and a separation of duties for who can pull exports. Do you support role-tiered access?
[10:54] Adam Reed: Yes, RBAC is supported with roles for auditors, ops, and developers. We also support time-limited export tokens for auditors.
[11:06] Marta Alvarez: One more: chain-of-custody proof — you mentioned signing with KMS. Is the signing performed within the customer's KMS so Redwood never sees the signing key?
[11:18] Priya Nair: For Dedicated/Private yes — we can have the manifest signed by your KMS, Redwood only provides the unsigned artifact. For Hosted, we offer Redwood-signed artifacts or a cross-account KMS flow.
[11:33] Samir Patel: We might need attestations from a third-party to satisfy risk. Do customers ever ask Redwood for a sub-processor list and contracts?
[11:43] Adam Reed: Yes, we maintain a sub-processor list and can share contracts under NDA.
[11:50] Michael O'Neal: About live incident response — if there's a suspected leak, what's the escalation path and how do we get forensic artifacts quickly?
[11:59] Priya Nair: We have a designated incident response flow; we'll provide a runbook. For Dedicated/Private customers, we can grant expedited access to raw logs or snapshots; for Hosted it's via support with SLA tiers.
[12:20] Marta Alvarez: Great. Could you walk us through the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of audit evidence ownership once — like bullet points.
[12:33] Priya Nair: Sure: Dedicated = Redwood-managed control plane but single-tenant compute and stronger separation; you can use customer KMS and private S3 buckets. Evidence can be generated in your account. Private = full customer control plane and infra, everything is in your environment, we package the software and you run it — most control for auditors.
[13:05] Speaker 1: Any cost delta implications for long-term retention and signing?
[13:12] Adam Reed: Retention cost scales with log volume. Signing itself is minimal cost but managing long-term storage (S3 Glacier/IA) will be the main contributor. We'll include cost scenarios in the estimate.
[13:28] Marta Alvarez: For the next call, our auditors want a sample exported artifact. Can Redwood produce a redacted sample export that mimics the real thing?
[13:38] Adam Reed: Yes, we'll produce a sample export with pii redacted and include the manifest/hash chain.
[13:45] Samir Patel: Also we'd like a technical deep dive focused on network setup and latency impact for dedicated vs hosted — Priya, can you lead that?
[13:53] Priya Nair: Yep, happy to. I'll propose times.
[14:00] Lena Ortiz: I'll coordinate calendar invites and share the SOC2 + pen test deck after the call.
[14:06] Marta Alvarez: Thanks — helpful. Quick clarifying Q: can Hosted support customer-managed KMS via cross-account key rotation? We have rotating keys and need to ensure past artifacts verify under historical keys.
[14:20] Priya Nair: We can support key rotation and maintain signed manifests with versioned keys. For full verification under historical keys, Dedicated/Private is simpler but Hosted can be configured.
[14:36] Speaker 4: Sorry interrupt — do you have example DSAR API calls?
[14:42] Adam Reed: Yes, we'll include API examples in the follow-up playbook.
[14:48] Marta Alvarez: Any other blockers from our side? I think we need the sample artifact, SOC2, and the network checklist.
[14:56] Adam Reed: Yup. We'll pack those up.
[15:00] Adam Reed: Alright, recap: send compliance pack + sample artifact, schedule tech deep dive, get topology from Samir, Marta to share auditor format. Anything else?
[15:12] Janelle Chu: No that's it, thanks.
[15:15] Michael O'Neal: Thanks all.
[15:18] Adam Reed: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up. End call.

Note: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KV cache noted as KV 'cash' in one segment), some speaker labels auto-assigned by the recorder.
